stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Set the initial angular velocity $\omega_0$ and angular acceleration $\alpha$, then press SPIN. Watch the tangential-velocity arrows at each marker as the disk turns. Fire at least three shots with two different $\omega_0$ values and move the $\alpha$ slider at least once.
stages.concept: Solid-body rotation: every point shares the same $\omega$ and $\alpha$. Tangential speed depends on radius: $v = r \cdot \omega$. Angular kinematics: $\omega(t) = \omega_0 + \alpha t$, $\theta(t) = \omega_0 t + \tfrac{1}{2}\alpha t^{2}$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Each target asks for a specific tangential speed at a specific marker. The live arrows show the current speed at each marker — tune $\omega_0$ and $\alpha$ so every marker hits its target speed at some moment during the spin.
stages.concept: For marker $k$ at radius $r_k$, hit condition is $r_k \cdot \omega(t_k) = v_k$ at some $t_k \in [0, T]$. Uniform rotation ($\alpha = 0$) hits every target only if all $v_k / r_k$ are equal; otherwise $\alpha \neq 0$ is needed to sweep $\omega$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The arrows are hidden. Read each target's marker, radius $r$ and required speed $v$. Compute the required $\omega = v/r$ for each, then choose $\omega_0$ and $\alpha$ so that $\omega(t) = \omega_0 + \alpha t$ passes through every value during $t \in [0, T]$. You have limited spins.
stages.concept: For a monotonic sweep from $\omega_a$ to $\omega_b$ over $T$: $\omega_0 = \omega_a$, $\alpha = (\omega_b - \omega_a)/T$. Any required $\omega^{*} \in [\omega_a, \omega_b]$ is reached at $t^{*} = (\omega^{*} - \omega_0)/\alpha$.

labels.tip1: set ω₀ and α, then SPIN — try two different ω₀ values
labels.tip2: watch each marker's arrow — hit when its length matches the target speed
labels.tip3: compute ω = v/r for each target, pick ω₀ and α, then SPIN
labels.peek_tip_vromega: Recall v = r·ω. For each target, the required angular velocity is ω = v/r.
labels.peek_tip_uniform: Uniform rotation (α = 0) hits every target only when all v/r ratios are equal.
labels.peek_tip_sweep: For a sweep: pick ω₀ = smallest required ω, then α = (largest − smallest)/T.

1.1: The vertical slider on the right sets ω₀; the horizontal slider at the bottom sets α.
1.2: Tangential arrows scale with r·ω — a marker further from the axis draws a longer arrow at the same ω.
1.3: Set α ≠ 0 and watch how the arrow lengths grow or shrink during a single spin.

2.1: For each target, the required ω satisfies r·ω = v_target. Read the target chip and compute.
2.2: If all required ω values are equal, set that ω₀ and leave α = 0.
2.3: Otherwise, sort the required ω values, put the smallest at ω₀ and set α so ω reaches the largest by t = T.

3.1: For each target: read r, read v_target, compute ω_k = v_target / r.
3.2: If the ω_k values are all equal, α = 0 and ω₀ = that value clears every target in one spin.
3.3: Sweep case: ω₀ = min(ω_k), α = (max(ω_k) − min(ω_k)) / T. Each ω_k is hit at t = (ω_k − ω₀)/α.
